assigned.title: Watchlist becomes usable: an add control and a list
assigned.acceptance: A person can add a title to their watchlist and see the list. The API and its mutation rules are complete, tested and reviewed -- including the conflict semantics in packages/persistence/src/watchlist-mutation.ts -- and nothing renders them. REQUIRED: the add control appears on the title screen and on a catalog card, and reflects state optimistically while remaining correct when the write is refused. REQUIRED: the resolution vocabulary the API already returns (accepted plus a reason, not a boolean ok) is surfaced honestly; a refused write must not render as a success, which is the shape of defect the harnesses in this repository have caught four times.

unit.evidence:
`npm run test` (turbo run test) at c63c8e8. Tasks: 22 successful, 22 total, exit 0. Measured
separately, `apps/web` alone is 78 test files / 1360 tests passed, exit 0.

52 of those are this task's four new suites:
  watchlist-state.test.ts      23  the decisions -- the optimistic flip, the four mutation reasons,
                                   the rollback on refused/unavailable/unreadable/listed
  watchlist-page-data.test.ts  13  the pure selection and all four branches of the server-side load,
                                   including that `no_active_profile_selected` is its own answer and
                                   that the catalog rights gate is applied to a watchlist entry
  watchlist-ui.test.tsx        12  the first paint via `react-dom/server`, the structural rules, and
                                   the verb guard described below
  watchlist-source.test.ts      4  the shared one-read-per-page snapshot

ONE EXISTING TEST WAS CHANGED AND IT WAS STRENGTHENED, NOT RELAXED.
`components/continue-watching/continue-watching-ui.test.tsx` asserted `expect(html).not.toContain
("<button")` on a resume card. PW-0304 mounts the My List toggle inside `CatalogCard`, so that line
began failing for a card that was behaving correctly -- it asserted an implementation (this card has
no buttons) rather than the property its own comment states (start over NAVIGATES, it does not
submit). Replaced by three assertions, each sharper than what it replaces: the href and the text are
now matched as ONE anchor element rather than as two independent `toContain`s; no `<button>` whose
text is "Start over"; and the one button a resume card may carry is named by its `data-testid`, so
the file states what it tolerates instead of tolerating any button. The surface amendment and this
reasoning were recorded as `task.definition_changed` before the file was touched.

A DEFECT THE UNIT LAYER DID NOT CATCH, RECORDED HERE BECAUSE THIS GATE IS WHY. `watchlistRequest`
sent `POST`; the route exports `PUT` and `DELETE` and answers 405 to a POST.
`watchlist-state.test.ts` asserted `POST` right beside the implementation, so this gate was green
while the control could not add anything. The e2e gate found it. `watchlist-ui.test.tsx` now reads
`app/api/v1/watchlist/[contentId]/route.ts` and asserts that every verb `watchlistRequest` can
produce is one that module exports, with a non-vacuity check on the extraction.

NOT A GATE ON THIS TASK AND NOT CLAIMED AS ONE: `npm run lint` (12/12, exit 0) and
`npm run repo:validate` (passed) were also run. `npm run format:check` fails on 538 files and did so
before this task; nothing here changed that and it is not asserted either way.

e2e.evidence:
`npx playwright test --project=chromium tests/watchlist.spec.ts` at c63c8e8, EXECUTED in three
configurations, exit 0 in all three. Browser: Chrome for Testing 151.0.7922.34, revision 1234 --
the build @playwright/test 1.62.1 pins, resolved from /root/.cache/ms-playwright (the container's
PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH points at a 1194 tree, which was NOT used; `critical-journey.spec.ts`
records why a shimmed revision is narrow local evidence rather than pinned-browser verification).

1. DEVELOPMENT, in-memory adapter, development-header identity.
   LIBERTY_E2E_WEB_MODE=development LIBERTY_E2E_PORT=3177
   7 passed, 4 skipped, exit 0. Covers: the nav entry is a link; the route serves 200 and names
   itself; the control's first paint is unpressable and says neither Add nor Remove; adding from a
   title page writes the row and the control still says so after a RELOAD; removing takes it away;
   a catalog card's control writes the card's own id and nothing else; and the refusal case below.

2. PRODUCTION, no database -- a deployment with no identity system.
   LIBERTY_E2E_PORT=3210
   3 passed, 8 skipped, exit 0. Asserts that this build refuses HONESTLY: the heading is "We
   couldn't load your list", the published reason is the one `src/env.ts` derives for the pinned
   variables (`storage_not_configured`), and "Nothing on your list yet" is absent -- the
   substitution that would tell a household their list is empty on the strength of never having
   read it.

3. PRODUCTION, REAL POSTGRESQL AND A REAL SIGNED-IN SESSION.
   LIBERTY_E2E_PORT=3200 LIBERTY_E2E_DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres@127.0.0.1:5433/lib_wl
   PostgreSQL 16.15, database created for this run and migrated with the repository's own
   `packages/persistence/migrations/0000_profile_scoped_identity.sql`. Sign-up and sign-in through
   `/api/auth/*` against that database; the session is a row, as PL-0401 requires.
   5 passed, 6 skipped, exit 0, AND RUN TWICE against the same (now non-empty) database to prove it
   is idempotent -- the second run also 5 passed / 6 skipped / exit 0. Covers: an entry written
   through the API is rendered on /watchlist, with the remove control, and clicking it removes the
   ROW (proved by a reload and by reading the API back); a viewer who is not signed in gets the
   sign-in panel carrying `next=%2Fwatchlist`; a signed-in viewer with no profile selected is sent
   to /profiles rather than to an error.

THE REFUSAL CASE IS REAL AND NOTHING IS INTERCEPTED. No `page.route`, no fulfilled response, no
planted attribute. The page loads as an identity that HAS selected a profile, so the control
resolves to a known "Add to My List" (asserted as a precondition -- a rollback from `unknown` would
be meaningless). The identity the PAGE sends is then changed to one that has selected nothing,
which is what a sign-out in another tab does to a page already on screen. The server answers its
own 403 `refused` envelope. Asserted: the status is 403; the control rolls back to "Add to My List"
with `aria-pressed="false"`; the notice reads the sentence that belongs to that reason code
("Choose a profile first."), not a generic failure; and the original identity's list is still empty
when read at the wire.

TWO TEST DEFECTS THIS GATE FOUND IN ITS OWN FIRST DRAFTS, recorded because they are the reason the
current assertions are shaped as they are.
  (a) THE CLIENT USED THE WRONG VERB. `watchlistRequest` sent `POST`; the route exports `PUT` and
      answers 405. The unit suite asserted `POST` beside the implementation and was green. Fixed in
      the client, and `watchlist-ui.test.tsx` now reads the route module so the unit layer can
      catch it next time.
  (b) THE FIRST DRAFT ASSERTED THE OPTIMISTIC STATE AND CALLED IT THE SETTLED ONE. `click()` then
      `toHaveText("Remove from My List")` is satisfied before anything is sent. It then reloaded
      while the write was still in flight -- the first PUT of a `next dev` process compiles the
      route and took ~400ms -- read a list the write had not reached, and failed. The product was
      right and the test was wrong: it had asserted a state the control publishes in order to say
      "I have not finished". Every press now arms `page.waitForResponse` BEFORE clicking, returns
      the status so the caller states which it expected, and asserts `aria-busy="false"` so the
      control's own account of being finished must agree with the network's. Nothing sleeps.

WHAT THIS GATE DOES NOT COVER, STATED RATHER THAN IMPLIED.
  - Only the `chromium` project ran. webkit, firefox and mobile-safari are in `playwright.config.ts`
    and were NOT executed; only chromium 1234 is installed in this container. UNVERIFIED on the
    other three engines.
  - Configuration 1 cannot observe the LIST PAGE at all, and that is the pre-existing defect filed
    as `defect.found` this round: the in-memory repository is instantiated once per Next module
    graph, so nothing written through /api/v1/* is visible to a server component. The spec states
    this in a skip reason rather than omitting the tests, and configuration 3 is what asserts the
    list page. PW-0305's continue-watching rail is affected identically and silently; the
    reproduction is in the event.
  - Configuration 3 has no catalog metadata source, so the entry it renders is the `item: null`
    branch ("A title we can't name right now") rather than a named card. A single configuration
    with BOTH a real database and a catalog does not exist in this harness today. Named cards on
    the list page are therefore UNVERIFIED end to end; the branch that produces them is covered by
    `watchlist-page-data.test.ts` and the card itself is `CatalogCard`, unchanged.
  - Nothing here was run on Windows and nothing here claims anything about Windows.

recommended.title: Series navigation and the next episode
recommended.acceptance: A viewer can move through a series without going back to the catalog. Today every season of a series renders as one flat stack on the title page, with no season selector, no per-episode progress and no way to reach the next episode. REQUIRED: season navigation that does not lose the viewer's place. REQUIRED: per-episode watched and in-progress state from the progress API. REQUIRED: a next-episode affordance at the end of playback, honouring the SAME per-episode rights gate the episode list already applies -- an autoplay that skips the rights check would be the rights breach PL-0703 was opened for, in a new place. REQUIRED: the next-episode selection rule is a pure function with its own tests, not logic inside a component, because 'what plays next' is exactly the kind of decision this project requires to be reconstructible.

recommended.title: Offline, degraded and error states a desktop application needs
recommended.acceptance: The application behaves honestly when the network, the backend or the sidecar is unavailable. There is no offline handling of any kind today -- no navigator.onLine, no service worker, no offline banner, no retry-on-reconnect. THIS MATTERS MORE ON THE DESKTOP THAN IT DID ON THE WEB: docs/DESKTOP_PLAYBACK.md section 8 accepts that an offline desktop cannot resolve playback at all, and requires that failure be surfaced as an honest unavailable outcome rather than an empty candidate list -- so the UI half of that ruling is this task. REQUIRED: a network-state signal and a visible degraded mode that names what is unavailable. REQUIRED: recovery on reconnect without a manual reload. REQUIRED: the sidecar being down is a DISTINCT state from the backend being down and from the network being down, because the three have different remedies and collapsing them produces a support burden. REQUIRED: no state invents content; an offline home shows what it has and says so.
